record_scope_reconstruction: Two distinct transit road gates: Tsamiya–Segbana on Nigeria–Benin and Kamba–Tunga Jado on Nigeria–Niger. This is a Cotonou-to-Niger trucking corridor, not the direct Benin–Niger border.

source_checks.finding: NAN account identifies two posts, actual truck clearance, and passage via Kamba toward Tunga Jado on February 9; closure onset remains unspecified.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Modal scope: multiple_sites. Only the reported 2026 transit-truck restriction; do not inherit 2019 national border regime.
unresolved: No independently sourced coordinate for either exact road gate recovered. Searches identify towns and planned infrastructure, insufficient to locate historical controls.

Native qualification: NAN and contemporary Nigerian local reporting quote the customs controller describing the Nigerian reopening decision and actual February 9, 2026 truck clearance; NAN also quotes a Niger representative welcoming that decision. Anadolu independently attributes the months-long measure to Nigeria. This supports recording Nigerian involvement, rather than treating it as solely Niger-imposed.

Banouto attributes the preceding blockage to Niger while describing the Nigerian reopening. Its disagreement remains visible; separate concurrent measures may have been conflated. No original closure order or precise onset was recovered. Officials’ descriptions of months of disruption establish a >24-hour restriction, but neither the three-month shorthand nor broad seven-year retrospective accounts establish an exact continuous interval. The 2019 trade regime, 2022 Kamba permission and direct Benin–Niger frontier restriction remain separate.
